**Summary**

I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and no money left the account). The quote at the time was $222.70 last / $222.72 ask, so the limit was ~0.1% above market, consistent with the "close to current market price" requirement. The fundamental case rests on Apple's fiscal 2024 results (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024, reported Oct 31 and filed in the 10-K on Nov 1): Q4 revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year revenue of $391.0 billion, net income of $93.7 billion, diluted EPS of $6.08 (including a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge), and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion — a highly cash-generative business with returning growth. News flow was neutral-to-mildly positive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual, staged rollout of Apple Intelligence, which is a potential multi-year upgrade catalyst but also a source of near-term uncertainty (I treated several low-quality "roundup" pages and a quarantined snippet containing unverifiable figures as noise and did not rely on them). Given solid reported fundamentals, strong cash generation, and a price essentially at market with no evidence of deterioration, I judged a modest starter position appropriate rather than passing; the main risks I'm accepting are soft iPhone 16 demand signals and the slow pace of Apple Intelligence feature availability.
